endorsements.quote: Researchers at the workshop emphasized the importance of considering each stakeholders ’ unique needs and tailoring information sharing to those needs, suggesting an opportunity for a human-centered design approach to transparency.

Workshop participants stated that it is important for users to be aware of the population represented in the data used to develop and validate the AI/ML device, including associated physical or social characteristics.

unlisted_practices: FDA should complement manufacturer-oriented device information with plain-language summaries and graphics targeted to non-manufacturer stakeholders.
Manufacturers should provide reliable mechanisms for users to report device malfunction and performance drift.
Manufacturers should work with the FDA on transparent communications regarding AI/ML devices.
Developers should communicate information using language and media appropriate for differing literacy, technical literacy, health literacy levels, and learning styles.
Stakeholders should establish a common framework and language around AI/ML devices to educate users.
Health systems should use standard notation in electronic health records to indicate AI/ML device use.
Patients should be provided educational resources including questions to ask their healthcare provider about AI/ML devices.

screen.reason: This is a commentary or perspective article discussing transparency and governance of AI/ML-enabled medical devices.
